newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Brazzaville radio airs pro-Sassou message.
newsitem.headline: Brazzaville radio airs pro-Sassou message.

text.p: A broadcast on Congo-Brazzaville's main state radio frequency declared on Monday evening that the militia of former president Denis Sassou Nguesso controlled most of the capital.

Sassou Nguesso's followers have been fighting the troops of President Pascal Lissouba for five days in a political and ethnic conflict which exploded as the country approached a presidential election set for July 27.

"Sassou's forces have repelled the forces of Lissouba and are controlling most of the city," said the broadcast, heard across the Congo River in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the recently renamed Zaire. "All police posts are under the control of Sassou."

The broadcast appeared to mean that the state radio building had been captured by Sassou's militia but there was no direct confirmation of this and the frequency might have been used by another transmitter.
The sound of heavy weapons fire indicated that fighting was continuing in the city.
